sequence.detail: Run every control total in the counts panel below against what was actually captured, before anyone leaves the session. Catching a short extract on day one is cheap; catching it in week three is not.

blockers.title: Fortellis subscription / App-Id is a separate entitlement from a DMS user login
blockers.detail: A CDK Drive admin login proves you can click around the DMS UI. It does not prove the dealer has an active Fortellis Subscription-Id or that our App-Id has been granted access to the specific APIs (Get Repair Order v3, Get Customer v3, Async Parts Inventory, FI Sales History) this plan depends on. These are provisioned separately, often by a different CDK team, and can take days.
blockers.ask: Ask CDK or Luke: confirm today whether a Fortellis production Subscription-Id already exists for Peterbilt Atlantic, and whether our registered App-Id is already entitled to Get Repair Order v3, Get Customer v3, Async Parts Inventory, and FI Sales History Bulk/Delta. If not, start that provisioning request now, in parallel with the DMS login — do not wait for one to finish before starting the other.

blockers.title: Export permissions are not the same as view permissions
blockers.detail: CDK Drive screens routinely let a user view a report on-screen without granting the 'export to file' or 'print to CSV' action — that is a separate permission bit tied to the user's role/security group.
blockers.ask: Ask CDK or Luke: confirm the admin login's security group includes export/print rights on the accounting-schedule screens, the GL journal inquiry screens, and the report writer — not just view rights. If the login is a fresh admin account, ask them to explicitly enable export on those three areas before the session starts.

blockers.title: Rooftop / Department-Id scoping can silently narrow what a pull returns
blockers.detail: Every Fortellis call is scoped by Subscription-Id and Department-Id headers. A pull run against one rooftop's Department-Id will not include the other 8 — there is no 'give me everything' header value documented.
blockers.ask: Ask CDK or Luke: get the full list of Department-Id values for all 9 Peterbilt Atlantic rooftops before the session starts, so every pull can be looped across all of them rather than discovered as a gap after the fact.

blockers.title: Row limits on screen-driven report exports
blockers.detail: Legacy DMS report screens (the ones behind GL journal detail, accounting schedules, warranty claims, and purchase/receipt documents — none of which have a public API) commonly cap export row counts or paginate silently, which can truncate a 3-month pull without an obvious error.
blockers.ask: Ask CDK or Luke: confirm the row/date-range limit on each report screen used for ledger and schedule export, and whether a 3-month pull needs to be run as three separate 1-month exports to stay under the cap.

integrity.control: Total RO count for the window, plus closed-RO dollars broken out by pay type (Customer / Warranty / Internal), reconciled against the RO status field.
integrity.proves: Every RO opened in the window was captured and none were double-counted or dropped on close.

integrity.control: Journal line count for the window, and debit total = credit total at the batch and period level.
integrity.proves: The ledger export is complete and internally balanced before it is used as the tie-out source of truth.

integrity.control: Schedule open-item total per control account (WIP schedule, warranty receivable schedule, floor-plan schedule) reconciled against the GL account balance it backs.
integrity.proves: Every schedule ties to its GL account — the exact test Phase 3 tie-out depends on.

integrity.control: Sale count and total sale amount for the window, split retail vs. wholesale, reconciled against parts-master on-hand quantity movement.
integrity.proves: Counter sales (which have no dedicated Fortellis API) were fully captured from screen export.

integrity.control: Finalized-deal count for the window with front-end and back-end gross totals, reconciled against FI Sales History bulk output.
integrity.proves: Every funded deal in the window is present, distinguishing finalized deals from We-Owes still pending.

integrity.control: Claim count and claimed-dollar total for the window, reconciled against the warranty receivable schedule balance.
integrity.proves: Claims submitted to PACCAR match what the schedule shows as still outstanding vs. paid.

targets.luke_name: Who can actually see and export what
targets.source_route: Screen report (Security/User Setup) + Fortellis Subscriptions API
targets.endpoint_or_screen: DMS User Setup / Security Group screen; Fortellis Subscriptions API (subscription status, App-Id entitlements)
targets.volume: 1 pull — one-time inventory, not a per-period volume

targets.luke_name: The chart of accounts — every account number everything posts to
targets.source_route: Screen report (Chart of Accounts screen)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: Accounting > Chart of Accounts screen — print/export to file
targets.volume: 200–600 accounts (base account × department suffix × sub-account letter combinations) for a 9-rooftop group
targets.control_key: Base account number + department suffix + sub-account letter

targets.luke_name: The control-sheet definitions — what has to match each GL balance
targets.source_route: Screen report (Schedule Setup / Accounting Schedules screen)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: Accounting > Schedules setup screen — one export per control account
targets.volume: 15–40 schedule definitions (WIP, warranty receivable, floor plan, and similar, per rooftop where scoped)

targets.luke_name: The department list — New Trucks, Used Trucks, Parts, Service, Body Shop
targets.source_route: Screen report (Department setup) + Fortellis header inventory
targets.endpoint_or_screen: Accounting > Department setup screen; cross-check against Department-Id header list per rooftop
targets.volume: 5–8 departments × 9 rooftops = 45–72 rows

targets.luke_name: The job codes and pay types techs and advisors pick from
targets.source_route: Screen report (Labor Operation Code setup)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: Service > Labor Operation Code setup screen — export code list
targets.volume: 300–1,500 op codes depending on how much of the PACCAR flat-rate manual is loaded locally

targets.luke_name: The parts pricing rules — source codes, MCD percentages
targets.source_route: Screen report (Parts pricing setup)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: Parts > Pricing/Source Code setup screen
targets.volume: 10–30 source/price codes

targets.luke_name: The list of document types the DMS tracks
targets.source_route: Screen report (System document type setup)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: System setup > Document type list — export
targets.volume: 20–50 document types

targets.luke_name: The customer record — fleet account, walk-in owner, or company
targets.source_route: Fortellis REST
targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Drive Get Customer v3 (bulk/delta)
targets.volume: 2,000–8,000 active customer records across 9 rooftops (fleet accounts + walk-ins, cumulative, not per-period)

targets.luke_name: The truck record — VIN, stock number, who owns it

targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Drive Service Vehicles API; Inventory > Unit lookup screen for stock number cross-reference

targets.luke_name: Who did the work — advisor, tech, cashier, parts counter person
targets.source_route: Fortellis REST (nested in RO payload) + screen export (Get Employee)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Get Employee; CDKDrive Repair Orders v1 (Query technicians / Query service advisors)
targets.volume: 80–250 active employee identifiers across 9 rooftops

targets.luke_name: Who we owe money to — PACCAR, sublet shops, everyone else
targets.source_route: Screen report (Vendor workflow / AP module)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: Accounting > Vendor workflow screen — view/export vendor list
targets.volume: 50–200 vendor records (PACCAR entities, sublet shops, general trade suppliers)

targets.luke_name: The parts bin record — what we have, where, and what it's worth
targets.source_route: Fortellis REST (async bulk)
targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Drive Async Parts Inventory API
targets.volume: 15,000–60,000 active part numbers on hand across 9 rooftops (snapshot, not per-period)

targets.luke_name: The RO you open when a truck rolls in — header
targets.source_route: Fortellis REST
targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Drive Get Repair Order v3 (bulk/delta, closed ROs)
targets.volume: 3,000–9,000 ROs opened across the 3-month window at a 9-rooftop truck dealer (roughly 110–330 ROs per rooftop per month)

targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Drive Get Repair Order v3 (line.laborOperations[])

targets.luke_name: One part on the RO — what it cost us, what we charged, whether it's a core
targets.source_route: Fortellis REST
targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Drive Get Repair Order v3 (line.parts[])

targets.luke_name: The tech's clock — when they punched in/out on a job

targets.endpoint_or_screen: CDK Drive Get Repair Order v3 (technicianPunchTimes[])

targets.luke_name: A straight parts-counter sale — no RO attached

targets.endpoint_or_screen: Parts > Counter Sales / Closed Sales report screen — export by date range

targets.luke_name: The claim we submit to PACCAR to get paid back for warranty work

targets.luke_name: The actual debit/credit entry that lands in the books

targets.luke_name: The running total of every open RO's cost, before it's billed out

targets.luke_name: The control sheet balances that have to match the GL account every month-end
